title: Classify T2 built-in trackpads as internal
author: Drecullith
body:
## Summary

Fix `disable_while_typing` on T2 MacBooks by marking Apple's built-in trackpad as an internal touchpad in the systemd hardware database.

On T2 machines, the internal keyboard/trackpad is exposed through the `t2bce_vhci` virtual USB controller. That makes the built-in trackpad appear removable/external to libinput, so its disable-while-typing feature is unavailable even when Hyprland has `input:touchpad:disable_while_typing` enabled.

This change adds a narrowly scoped hwdb override:

- matches Apple's USB vendor;
- matches the specific `Apple Inc. Apple Internal Keyboard / Trackpad` device name;
- marks it with `ID_INPUT_TOUCHPAD_INTEGRATION=internal`;
- does not hard-code one USB product ID, allowing the rule to cover T2 model variants and product-ID changes;
- does not match an external Apple Magic Trackpad.

Fresh T2 installs deploy and compile the rule through the existing `fix-t2.sh` hardware path.

A new migration applies the same rule to existing T2 installations, using the same T2 PCI detection already used by Omarchy's T2 setup. The migration only recompiles the hwdb when the installed rule differs from the shipped rule, making it idempotent.

The input-device retrigger is best-effort. Updating the udev properties does not guarantee that libinput recreates an already-open device in the running compositor, so existing users whose migration installs the rule are told to log out and back in or reboot before testing disable-while-typing.

Fixes #10815.

## Tests

Added `test/shell.d/t2-trackpad-test.sh` covering:

- fresh T2 setup installs and activates the hwdb rule;
- the reported `05ac:027b` internal trackpad is classified as internal;
- another T2 product ID, `05ac:027e`, is also classified as internal;
- hardware-validated `05ac:0340` is classified as internal;
- an external Apple Magic Trackpad does not match the override;
- existing T2 installations receive the migration;
- repaired existing installs receive logout/login or reboot guidance;
- rerunning the migration with the current rule is a no-op and does not repeat that guidance;
- non-T2 systems are left untouched and receive no activation guidance.

The focused regression suite passes locally.

Also verified:

- `bash -n install/hardware/apple/fix-t2.sh`
- `bash -n migrations/1788912000.sh`
- `bash -n test/shell.d/t2-trackpad-test.sh`
- the shipped hwdb file compiles successfully with `systemd-hwdb --strict`

## Real-world validation

Real-hardware validation has now been performed on three T2 MacBook configurations.

### MacBookPro16,1 / `05ac:0340`

On a MacBookPro16,1 using Apple USB product `05ac:0340`, changing the built-in trackpad classification from `external` to `internal` made libinput disable-while-typing support become available and enabled.

The running compositor successfully paired disable-while-typing with the internal keyboard after the trackpad device was recreated.

That test used a controller-specific udev rule rather than this PR's installer or migration path. Separately, this PR's exact shipped hwdb rule was compiled with `systemd-hwdb --strict` and confirmed to match `05ac:0340` while leaving an external `05ac:0265` Magic Trackpad outside the override.

### MacBookPro15,2 / `05ac:027b`

Additional end-to-end validation was performed on a MacBookPro15,2 using Apple USB product `05ac:027b`, matching the model and controller from the original issue report.

The PR's hwdb rule was applied manually, the hwdb was rebuilt and the input subsystem retriggered, followed by a logout and fresh login.

Before the fix:

- `ID_INTEGRATION` reported `external`;
- `ID_INPUT_TOUCHPAD_INTEGRATION` reported `external`;
- resting a palm on the trackpad while typing reliably moved the cursor and/or produced accidental clicks.

After applying the rule and starting a fresh session:

- `ID_INTEGRATION` reported `internal`;
- `ID_INPUT_TOUCHPAD_INTEGRATION` reported `internal`;
- typing normally with a palm resting on the trackpad no longer moved the cursor or produced accidental clicks.

Hyprland's `input:touchpad:disable_while_typing` option was already `true` before and after the change, confirming that the problem was the trackpad's external classification rather than the compositor setting itself.

### MacBookPro16,2 / changing product ID

A third real-hardware test was performed on a MacBookPro16,2 using the same internal `Apple Inc. Apple Internal Keyboard / Trackpad` device through `t2bce_vhci`.

Before applying the rule:

- `ID_INPUT_TOUCHPAD_INTEGRATION` reported `external`;
- Hyprland's `input:touchpad:disable_while_typing` setting was already `true`, but had no practical effect;
- resting a palm on the trackpad while typing caused cursor movement and accidental input.

After applying this PR's exact name-matched hwdb rule and starting a fresh session:

- `ID_INPUT_TOUCHPAD_INTEGRATION` reported `internal`;
- Hyprland's DWT setting became effective;
- the Hyprland/libinput log confirmed DWT activation;
- palm contact while typing no longer caused cursor movement or accidental input.

This machine also provided an important validation of the rule's matching strategy.

The same physical trackpad appeared as USB product `05ac:027e` before one reboot and `05ac:034a` afterward. A rule pinned to enumerated product IDs could therefore stop matching the device across reboots.

Because this PR instead matches Apple's USB vendor together with the exact internal keyboard/trackpad device name, the rule continued to classify the device correctly across both product IDs.

This supports keeping the shipped rule product-ID-independent rather than attempting to enumerate every observed T2 controller ID.

## Activation behavior

The hardware tests consistently support the activation behavior documented by the migration.

An `action=change` retrigger can update the udev properties, but does not guarantee that libinput recreates an already-open device in the running compositor.

Logging out and back in or rebooting provides reliable device re-enumeration before testing disable-while-typing.

## Acknowledgements

Thanks to @dlpwaters for the MacBookPro16,1 hardware validation, before/after libinput measurements, verification of the `05ac:0340` controller, and for identifying the need to give existing users explicit logout/login or reboot guidance after migration.

Thanks to @igorski89 for independently validating the fix end-to-end on the original MacBookPro15,2 / `05ac:027b` hardware and confirming the user-visible result with a practical palm-while-typing test.

Thanks also to @RFdeGroot for validating the exact rule on a MacBookPro16,2 and identifying that the same physical trackpad can expose different USB product IDs across reboots, providing direct real-world evidence for the product-ID-independent matching strategy.

Together, those tests provide end-to-end confirmation across multiple T2 MacBook variants and strengthen confidence that the rule restores disable-while-typing without relying on unstable product-ID enumeration.

files.patch:
@@ -26,6 +26,14 @@ if lspci -nn | grep "106b:180[12]" >/dev/null; then
   echo "MODULES+=(t2bce_vhci usbhid hid_apple hid_generic xhci_pci xhci_hcd)" > \
     /etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d/apple-t2.conf
 
+  # The same virtual USB bridge makes the built-in trackpad look removable to
+  # libinput. Mark only Apple's Internal Keyboard / Trackpad device as internal
+  # so disable-while-typing is available without affecting external trackpads.
+  install -Dm644 "$OMARCHY_PATH/install/hardware/apple/t2-trackpad.hwdb" \
+    /etc/udev/hwdb.d/71-omarchy-t2-trackpad.hwdb
+  systemd-hwdb update
+  udevadm trigger --subsystem-match=input --action=change || true
+
   mkdir -p /etc/limine-entry-tool.d
   cat > /etc/limine-entry-tool.d/t2-mac.conf <<'EOF'
 # Generated by Omarchy installer for T2 Mac support

@@ -0,0 +1,5 @@
+# The T2 virtual USB bridge makes the built-in MacBook trackpad look removable.
+# Match the internal composite device by name so product-ID differences between
+# T2 models do not disable libinput's disable-while-typing support.
+touchpad:usb:v05acp*:name:Apple Inc. Apple Internal Keyboard / Trackpad:*
+ ID_INPUT_TOUCHPAD_INTEGRATION=internal

@@ -0,0 +1,19 @@
+echo "Mark T2 MacBook built-in trackpads as internal"
+
+source_hwdb="$OMARCHY_PATH/install/hardware/apple/t2-trackpad.hwdb"
+target_hwdb="${OMARCHY_T2_TRACKPAD_HWDB:-/etc/udev/hwdb.d/71-omarchy-t2-trackpad.hwdb}"
+
+# Existing T2 installs already passed the hardware installer, so repair them on
+# update. Keep the same PCI gate as fix-t2.sh and only rebuild the hwdb when the
+# shipped rule differs from what is installed.
+if lspci -nn | grep "106b:180[12]" >/dev/null; then
+  if ! cmp -s "$source_hwdb" "$target_hwdb"; then
+    sudo install -Dm644 "$source_hwdb" "$target_hwdb"
+    sudo systemd-hwdb update
+    # A failed live retrigger is non-fatal. Even a successful action=change may
+    # not recreate libinput's existing device, so a new session is the reliable
+    # point at which the static integration property is consumed.
+    sudo udevadm trigger --subsystem-match=input --action=change || true
+    echo "Log out and back in or reboot to activate disable-while-typing on the internal trackpad."
+  fi
+fi

@@ -0,0 +1,129 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+
+set -euo pipefail
+source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"
+
+fix_t2="$ROOT/install/hardware/apple/fix-t2.sh"
+hwdb="$ROOT/install/hardware/apple/t2-trackpad.hwdb"
+migration="$ROOT/migrations/1788912000.sh"
+
+require_command systemd-hwdb
+
+# Fresh T2 installs must deploy the same rule that the migration uses, compile
+# the hwdb, and try to refresh existing input devices immediately.
+grep -Fq 'install -Dm644 "$OMARCHY_PATH/install/hardware/apple/t2-trackpad.hwdb"' "$fix_t2" ||
+  fail "fresh T2 setup installs the internal-trackpad hwdb rule"
+grep -Fq 'systemd-hwdb update' "$fix_t2" ||
+  fail "fresh T2 setup compiles the updated hwdb"
+grep -Fq 'udevadm trigger --subsystem-match=input --action=change || true' "$fix_t2" ||
+  fail "fresh T2 setup retriggers input devices without making install depend on it"
+pass "fresh T2 setup installs and activates the trackpad classification"
+
+test_tmp=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -rf "$test_tmp"' EXIT
+
+# Validate the actual shipped rule with systemd-hwdb. Product IDs differ across
+# T2 models, while the built-in composite device name stays specific enough not
+# to match an external Magic Trackpad. 0340 is hardware-validated on a
+# MacBookPro16,1 in addition to the originally reported controller IDs.
+hwdb_root="$test_tmp/hwdb-root"
+mkdir -p "$hwdb_root/etc/udev/hwdb.d"
+cp "$hwdb" "$hwdb_root/etc/udev/hwdb.d/71-omarchy-t2-trackpad.hwdb"
+systemd-hwdb --root="$hwdb_root" --strict update
+
+query_hwdb() {
+  systemd-hwdb --root="$hwdb_root" query "$1" 2>/dev/null || true
+}
+
+for product in 027b 027e 0340; do
+  result=$(query_hwdb "touchpad:usb:v05acp${product}:name:Apple Inc. Apple Internal Keyboard / Trackpad:")
+  grep -Fxq 'ID_INPUT_TOUCHPAD_INTEGRATION=internal' <<<"$result" ||
+    fail "T2 internal trackpad product $product is classified as internal" "$result"
+done
+pass "known T2 internal trackpads match the shipped hwdb rule"
+
+magic=$(query_hwdb 'touchpad:usb:v05acp0265:name:Apple Inc. Magic Trackpad:')
+! grep -q 'ID_INPUT_TOUCHPAD_INTEGRATION=internal' <<<"$magic" ||
+  fail "external Magic Trackpad is not classified as internal" "$magic"
+pass "external Magic Trackpad stays outside the T2 override"
+
+# Existing installs are repaired by a new migration, and rerunning it after the
+# file is current must be a no-op.
+stub_bin="$test_tmp/bin"
+calls="$test_tmp/calls.log"
+migration_output="$test_tmp/migration.out"
+target_hwdb="$test_tmp/etc/udev/hwdb.d/71-omarchy-t2-trackpad.hwdb"
+mkdir -p "$stub_bin"
+: >"$calls"
+
+cat >"$stub_bin/lspci" <<'SH'
+#!/bin/bash
+if (( ${T2_HARDWARE:-0} == 1 )); then
+  echo '01:00.0 Bridge [0680]: Apple Inc. T2 Security Chip [106b:1801]'
+else
+  echo '00:00.0 Host bridge [0600]: Example [ffff:0000]'
+fi
+SH
+
+cat >"$stub_bin/sudo" <<'SH'
+#!/bin/bash
+printf 'sudo' >>"$TEST_LOG"
+printf '\t%s' "$@" >>"$TEST_LOG"
+printf '\n' >>"$TEST_LOG"
+"$@"
+SH
+
+cat >"$stub_bin/systemd-hwdb" <<'SH'
+#!/bin/bash
+printf 'systemd-hwdb' >>"$TEST_LOG"
+printf '\t%s' "$@" >>"$TEST_LOG"
+printf '\n' >>"$TEST_LOG"
+SH
+
+cat >"$stub_bin/udevadm" <<'SH'
+#!/bin/bash
+printf 'udevadm' >>"$TEST_LOG"
+printf '\t%s' "$@" >>"$TEST_LOG"
+printf '\n' >>"$TEST_LOG"
+SH
+
+chmod +x "$stub_bin"/*
+
+run_migration() {
+  PATH="$stub_bin:$PATH" \
+    TEST_LOG="$calls" \
+    T2_HARDWARE="$1" \
+    OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" \
+    OMARCHY_T2_TRACKPAD_HWDB="$target_hwdb" \
+    bash -euo pipefail "$migration" >"$migration_output"
+}
+
+run_migration 1
+cmp -s "$hwdb" "$target_hwdb" ||
+  fail "T2 migration installs the exact shipped hwdb rule"
+grep -Fq $'systemd-hwdb\tupdate' "$calls" ||
+  fail "T2 migration recompiles the hwdb" "$(cat "$calls")"
+grep -Fq $'udevadm\ttrigger\t--subsystem-match=input\t--action=change' "$calls" ||
+  fail "T2 migration retriggers input devices" "$(cat "$calls")"
+grep -Fq 'Log out and back in or reboot to activate disable-while-typing' "$migration_output" ||
+  fail "T2 migration tells existing users when a new session is required" "$(cat "$migration_output")"
+pass "T2 migration repairs existing installs and explains activation"
+
+: >"$calls"
+run_migration 1
+[[ ! -s $calls ]] ||
+  fail "T2 migration is idempotent once the rule is current" "$(cat "$calls")"
+! grep -Fq 'Log out and back in or reboot to activate disable-while-typing' "$migration_output" ||
+  fail "T2 migration does not repeat activation guidance when no repair was needed" "$(cat "$migration_output")"
+pass "T2 migration leaves an already-current rule alone"
+
+rm -f "$target_hwdb"
+: >"$calls"
+run_migration 0
+[[ ! -e $target_hwdb ]] ||
+  fail "non-T2 systems do not receive the trackpad override"
+[[ ! -s $calls ]] ||
+  fail "non-T2 systems skip hwdb activation" "$(cat "$calls")"
+! grep -Fq 'Log out and back in or reboot to activate disable-while-typing' "$migration_output" ||
+  fail "non-T2 systems do not receive T2 activation guidance" "$(cat "$migration_output")"
+pass "T2 migration skips unrelated hardware"

comments.body:
Additional live hardware validation on **MacBookPro16,1 / Apple USB `05ac:0340`**: correcting the trackpad's external classification made disable-while-typing available and enabled.

[Full diagnosis, tested local rule, application/undo steps, and before/after measurements](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/issues/10815#issuecomment-5646369349).

On Omarchy `4.0.3-1`, Hyprland `0.56.2-2`, libinput `1.31.3-1`, and systemd `261.2-1`:

- Hyprland's DWT option was already `true`.
- Both udev integration properties changed from `external` to `internal`.
- `libinput_device_config_dwt_is_available()` changed from `0` to `1`.
- `libinput_device_config_dwt_get_default_enabled()` changed from `0` to `1`.
- After a targeted trackpad remove/add notification, the running compositor reopened it and logged DWT pairing with the internal keyboard. The keyboard stayed connected and `hyprctl configerrors` was empty.

The live test used the controller-specific udev rule documented in the issue comment, **not this PR's installer or migration**. Separately, I compiled this PR's exact hwdb file from `f768552b8317e3c9588cbb46aebdf5c3952ccdcf` with `systemd-hwdb --strict` in an isolated root. Its wildcard matched `05ac:0340` and returned no override for an external `05ac:0265` Magic Trackpad query.

Two useful follow-ups:

1. Add `0340` to the hwdb regression cases as another hardware-validated controller.
2. Tell existing users to log out/in or reboot after migration. An `action=change` retrigger updates udev properties, but libinput reads those static properties when adding the device; it does not guarantee the existing compositor device is recreated. A Hyprland config reload alone is insufficient to guarantee activation.

@dlpwaters Thank you — this was very useful validation.

I've updated the branch to incorporate both follow-ups:

- "05ac:0340" is now included in the hwdb regression cases as a hardware-validated T2 controller alongside "027b" and "027e";
- when the migration actually installs the rule on an existing T2 system, it now tells the user to log out and back in or reboot before testing disable-while-typing, since an "action=change" retrigger does not guarantee libinput recreates the existing device.

The regression also checks that this activation guidance is not repeated on an already-current install and is not shown on non-T2 systems.

Local syntax checks and the focused shell regression pass.

New head: "9890cbaf4be3f2cc1be1d1b1a911fbb2a0b36798"

Thanks again for the real-hardware measurements and for catching the session-lifetime caveat.

Additional real-hardware confirmation on a **MacBookPro15,2** / `05ac:027b` — the same model and controller as the original issue report, and one of the product IDs already covered by this PR's hwdb regression cases.

Applied this PR's exact hwdb rule manually (commit `9890cbaf`), rebooted, and ran a practical typing test rather than just checking the udev property: before the fix, resting a palm on the trackpad while typing reliably moved the cursor and/or clicked; after applying the rule and a fresh login, that stopped entirely.

Full write-up with before/after `ID_INPUT_TOUCHPAD_INTEGRATION` values and versions: https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/issues/10815#issuecomment-5687715036

Confirmed the fix works on a **MacBookPro16,2** (13", 2020, 4x Thunderbolt 3; board `Mac-5F9802EFE386AA28`).

### Environment

- Omarchy `4.0.4-1`
- Hyprland `0.56.2-2`
- libinput `1.31.3-1`
- systemd `261.2-1`
- Kernel `7.2.4-arch1-Watanare-T2-3-t2`
- Device: `Apple Inc. Apple Internal Keyboard / Trackpad`, via `t2bce_vhci`

### What I did

Applied this PR's exact `t2-trackpad.hwdb` rule (name-matched, not product-ID-specific) at `/etc/udev/hwdb.d/71-omarchy-t2-trackpad.hwdb`, then `systemd-hwdb update` + `udevadm trigger --subsystem-match=input --action=change`, then logged out/rebooted — consistent with the activation notes already in this thread.

### Before / after

| Property | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `ID_INPUT_TOUCHPAD_INTEGRATION` | `external` | `internal` |
| `hyprctl getoption input:touchpad:disable_while_typing` | `true` (no effect) | `true` (now effective) |

Hyprland's log confirms DWT actually engaging post-fix:

```
[libinput] event14 - palm: dwt activated with Apple Inc. Apple Internal Keyboard / Trackpad<->Apple Inc. Apple Internal Keyboard / Trackpad
```

### One extra data point for the name-vs-product-ID matching approach

On this machine the trackpad's USB product ID was **not stable across reboots**: `05ac:027e` before a reboot, `05ac:034a` after. A product-ID-pinned rule would have silently stopped matching here. This PR's device-name match handled both automatically, which is a good argument for keeping it that way rather than enumerating product IDs.

### Real-world result

Before: resting a palm on the trackpad while typing reliably moved the cursor / produced clicks. After: typing normally with a palm on the pad no longer moves the cursor or triggers accidental input. Matches the on-device behavior reported by @igorski89 above.

@igorski89 Thank you — this is excellent validation.

Testing the exact hwdb rule on a MacBookPro15,2 / "05ac:027b", matching the original reported hardware, closes an important gap in the real-world coverage.

The practical palm-while-typing test is especially useful because it confirms the classification change translates into the intended user-visible disable-while-typing behavior rather than only changing the udev property.

Your logout/login result also independently confirms the activation guidance added after @dlpwaters' testing: updating the property alone does not guarantee that libinput recreates the already-open device.

I'll add this MacBookPro15,2 / "027b" result to the PR's real-world validation notes.

Thanks for taking the time to test it properly.

@RFdeGroot Thank you — this is extremely useful validation.

The MacBookPro16,2 result gives us a third independently tested T2 configuration, and the practical palm-while-typing result confirms the classification change is translating into the intended disable-while-typing behavior.

The product-ID change from "05ac:027e" to "05ac:034a" across reboots is particularly valuable. That is strong real-world evidence for keeping the hwdb rule scoped by Apple's vendor and the exact internal keyboard/trackpad device name rather than enumerating product IDs, since an ID-pinned rule could have stopped matching the same physical machine after reboot.

Your logout/reboot result also lines up with the activation behavior already observed on the other hardware tests.

I'll add this MacBookPro16,2 result and the product-ID instability finding to the PR's real-world validation notes.

Thanks for testing it this thoroughly.

Automated duplication check: this pull request looks similar to #6928, which covers the same T2 trackpad internal tag. I keep that one open and close this one to consolidate review.

If you feel this is the wrong decision, please open the PR again with a note on the difference.
